items.title: Low pressure in US midwest brings unseasonable heat to New York and Boston
items.desc: Further south this week, severe thunderstorms affected midterms voting in Florida, Oklahoma and ColoradoDespite the rapid descent into autumn in the northern hemisphere, parts of eastern North America have experienced an exceptionally late taste of summer in recent days. Temperatures approached 23C (73F) in New York and Boston, about 7-10C above what is expected in early November. The unseasonable warmth spilled into parts of eastern Canada, with temperatures exceeding 20C, about 10-15C above normal for the time of year. The balmy conditions were caused by an area of low pressure in the US midwest, dragging up exceptionally warm air from the Gulf of Mexico along its eastern flank. This area of low pressure will gradually drift eastwards, allowing temperatures to fall closer to the average.Further south, severe thunderstorms have resulted in numerous flood warnings and evacuation warnings being issued this week across many states, with disruptive weather affecting polling stations in Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado. The powerful thunderstorms even resulted in a tornado touching down in Keyes, Oklahoma, forcing the relocation of a polling station. The tornado caused extensive damage, although no causalities have been reported. items.title: Europe: What we know about the hoax bomb threats disrupting flights
items.desc: Dozens of European flights have been disrupted this week after bomb threats were sent in to various airports, with fighter planes escorting many civilian aircraft after threats were called in mid-flight.

items.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults
items.desc: British comedian Russell Brand was on Thursday, November 5, found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults by a London jury, including a 16-year-old girl. He now faces "significant" prison time, according to the judge.

items.title: Pressure mounts on US Defence chief Hegseth after Republican election rout
items.desc: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is under growing pressure, with victorious Democrats planning to target him in Congress and Republicans blaming the Iran war he championed for their election losses. President Donald Trump has stood by Hegseth so far, insisting he's doing "a very good job".  But Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both blamed midterm election losses on the Iran war, for which Hegseth is a key advocate and spokesman.

items.title: 'Trump is a very dangerous person for the world': EU's former top diplomat Josep Borrell
items.desc: In an interview with Talking Europe, the EU's former top diplomat Josep Borrell reacts to the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, warning that US President Donald Trump is still "a very dangerous person for the world".

items.title: 'Chaos within aviation industry' as European air traffic hit by bomb threats
items.desc: Officials across Europe reported a fresh slew of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, November 6, following a string of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week. Two broadcasters also received security threats, in a possible sign the menace was spreading beyond the skies. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi has more.

items.title: Wounded French protesters to sue interior minister over police brutality
items.desc: Around ten demonstrators wounded at recent protests in France on Friday said they will sue Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over police brutality. Student and cost-of-living protests in recent weeks have been marred by violence, including reports of police inflicting serious and lifechanging injuries on protesters – many of whom are minors.

items.title: Turkey to push for 'electrification' drive at COP31 as climate threats mount
items.desc: COP31 host Turkey is set to push for a "electrification" drive to help meet global elergy demand as the UN climate conference kicks off in Antalya on Monday. The annual summit takes place this year under the shadow of a cost-of-living crisis fuelled by the war in the Middle East.

items.title: China keeps a close eye on US midterm shake
items.desc: The US midterm elections have resulted in the Democratic Party taking control of both chambers of the US Congress, leaving Donald Trump as a lame duck president for the remainder of his term. Professor Steve Tsang of the SOAS China Institute tells FRANCE 24 that, while a weakened Trump could strengthen Beijing's negotiating position, the Chinese leadership is aware that Congress has relatively little sway over foreign policy and is keen to maintain warm personal ties between the two presidents.

items.title: Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip with a first stop in Uruguay
items.desc: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America on Friday, November 6, with a visit to Uruguay, the region’s least Catholic and most secular country, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question. After Uruguay, he will then go to Argentina and Peru. FRANCE 24's Hanna Roberts has more.

items.title: California governor to grant clemency to all 548 death row inmates in state
items.desc: California's governor Gavy Newsom announced Thursday that he will commute all death sentences in the state to life without the possibility of parole. He said that "capital punishment is morally wrong." The state Supreme Court will have the final say in hundreds of those cases.

items.title: The women who rode the blue wave
items.desc: In this edition, we report on how the US midterms, which saw the Democrats make massive gains, also marked a series of historic firsts for women. Also the dark side to Bangkok's booming fertility industry, which attracts thousands of foreign patients seeking assistance from the Thai capital's state-of-the-art private clinics. Plus how an impoverished neighbourhood in El Salvador, once a no-go zone plagued by gang violence, is being transformed by women into a vibrant canvas for street art.

items.title: 'Too early to draw conclusions' as bomb threat hoaxes target European countries
items.desc: Several Irish media outlets reported receiving bomb threats on Friday as a wave of hoax alerts that had so far mainly targeted airlines continued across Europe, with more than a dozen new flights affected. No explosives have been found in any of the incidents so far. European authorities are scrambling to identify the sources of the threats, as FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating reports.

items.title: Paraguay's Peña offers resignation amid banking scandal, protests
items.desc: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation on Thursday, but Congress put it on hold as impeachment proceedings against him move forward. Peña is facing impeachment over a banking scandal that has affected millions of people and sparked protests, with thousands taking to the streets in recent days.

items.title: Trump’s stillborn diesel deal: Why Russian oil tankers are not heading to the US
items.desc: The first oil tankers scheduled to deliver Russian diesel to the US under a deal between President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin have changed course and are no longer heading toward the US coast. It spells the end of an agreement announced with great fanfare before the midterms.

items.title: Is Israel opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot going to replace Benjamin Netanyahu?
items.desc: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday, November 5, as the frontrunner to be tasked with forming a government. This comes after one of the two main parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters – a longtime ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition – declined to recommend any candidate for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky reports.

items.title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future in question after midterms setback
items.desc: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future is in question after Tuesday's, November 3, midterms setback. On Thursday, November 5, he issued a video message vowing to fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defending the ‌Iran war as “courageous and historic”. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

items.title: Tech giants lose $1 trillion in one day after Democrats victory in midterms
items.desc: Trillions of dollars have been wiped off the stock value of major tech firms in the US, Europe and Asia. Investors appear worried about the possibility of an AI slowdown and tougher regulation as Democrats won the midterms in the US. Some of the Democratic candidates had expressed their opposition to the data centres that are needed to power AI technology.

items.title: Canada PM Mark Carney unveils budget to strengthen economy
items.desc: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled his first ever budget on November 5, which set out strong ambitions for greater economic independence from the US. The "Masters of our Destiny" budget also announced generous measures for parts of the economy affected by tariffs, setting aside 44 billion Canadian dollars for impacted businesses and workers.

items.title: Will Democratic Party introduce a new 'New Deal'? Key narrative must be 'focused on economic issues'
items.desc: With Democrats poised to control both chambers of Congress, the party faces a defining challenge: how to constrain Donald Trump's presidency while carving out a path to the White House in 2028. For Ian Reifowitz, Distinguished Professor of History at SUNY Empire State University, the answer lies in drawing on the historical legacy of Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal coalition. Republicans, he argues, have progressively shifted electoral competition towards questions of identity, immigration and cultural conflict. Democrats, by contrast, must recover their traditional strength on economic security, affordability and everyday living standards. "These Democrats across the country ran on affordability." And that's how they must govern, explains Reifowitz.

items.title: 'Period of uncertainty: Trump is tormented, he's unstoppable, and he's desperate for immortality'
items.desc: François Picard is pleased to welcome Craig Copetas, Greek-American author, international affairs columnist and editor at Türkiye Today and French Senator Hélène Conway-Mouret. "What you have is a tormented and unstable president who's desperate for immortality." With this arresting assessment, Copetas captures what he considers the defining paradox of Donald Trump's presidency in the aftermath of the US midterm elections: a leader politically neutered at home but potentially emboldened on the international stage.

items.title: The human cost of recycling: Kenyan waste pickers put their health at risk
items.desc: Two thousand tonnes of waste are dumped every day at the Dandora landfill site in the Kenyan capital Nairobi. An army of workers then rush in to recover recyclable materials, putting their own health at risk in the process. But however hard these unsung environmental heroes work, only 7 percent of the plastic can be recycled. Our correspondents report.

items.title: Europe's crisis of discontent: Student and cost-of-living protests spread across EU
items.desc: A growing wave of discontent is sweeping across Europe. What began in France as student protests over deteriorating school conditions, teacher shortages and an education system under pressure has quickly grown into something much bigger: a groundswell of discontent over the rising cost of living, unaffordable housing and struggling public services.

items.title: 中东危机可能重塑亚太地区就业格局
items.desc: 国际劳工组织周四发布政策简报指出，中东危机导致的能源供应中断，暴露了亚太地区对进口化石燃料的依赖。随着各国加快发展清洁能源、保障能源安全，该地区就业格局可能发生重大变化。虽然可再生能源、储能和电气化领域的投资有望创造大量就业机会，但新增岗位未必能惠及因产业调整而失去工作的劳动者。

items.title: 发展中国家外债升至9.4万亿美元，创历史新高

items.title: “教育不能等待”基金6亿美元筹资目标近在咫尺
items.desc: 各国政府和合作伙伴周四在瑞士日内瓦举行的高级别补充筹资会议上，宣布向联合国全球紧急教育基金“教育不能等待”新增4.058亿美元承诺资金。加上此前通过多年期捐助承诺已获得的1.358亿美元，该基金“希望从这里开始”（Hope Starts Here）筹资活动累计获得5.416亿美元资金及承诺，达到6亿美元目标的90%。

items.title: 【专题报道 】驶向电气化未来：交通转型如何助力全球气候目标

items.title: COP31前瞻：今年联合国气候变化大会有哪些重要议题？
items.desc: 如今，全球拥有比以往更多的技术和手段来应对气候变化，但仍有数百万人无法从中受益。随着清洁能源技术以前所未有的速度发展，各国在第31届联合国气候变化大会上面临的挑战，已不再只是寻找解决方案，而是如何让所有人都有能力负担这些方案的成本。

items.title: 全球四分之一青少年过去一周每天运动均不足一小时

items.title: 全球升温恐将突破1.5℃温控红线

items.title: 阿富汗逾半数适龄儿童未接受正规小学教育
